title: The pane title, the check's label and its tip count F's sheets, not what the deformation draws, and call them sheets of H_t
detail: In the 'html' branch, sheetsClause ignores sh.hom, so the Landscape title reads "landscape of Im H_t, both sheets" / ", all 3 sheets" / ", 24 of 60 sheet combinations". K is F's (multiSheet() = GLR.sheetInfo(endMap())), not render3D.sheetsInfo, and the title calls them sheets of H_t. Three cases make it false. (a) At t = 0 there is one function, H_0 (sin z in the user's case), drawn as identical copies. (b) One after another, before a multivalued step begins, fewer surfaces are drawn. For √ then √ at T = 0.5, 2 surfaces are drawn under "all 4 sheets". For sin then ∛ at T = 0.5, sheetPlan returns null and one surface is drawn under "all 3 sheets". (c) For 0 < t < 1, z^s with s = 1 + (α − 1)t has infinitely many sheets for irrational s and q sheets for s = p/q, so "both sheets" of H_t is wrong as a statement about H_t. This is exactly the kind of wording the user objected to. sheetsLabel has the same problem: it shows F's "All sheets (24 of 60)" and the tip "24 of the 60 surfaces are drawn" while, for example, 12 are drawn (see math-5).
evidence: src/app.js 7473-7480: the html branch has no sh.hom case. src/app.js 7450-7465: sheetsShown takes K and total from multiSheet() (F's). Node probe (notes/v16-user5/review-math-probes/probe3.js) with Funcs.sheetMapCombos against Funcs.sheetCombos: sqrt-sqrt T=0.5 drawn K 2, F K 4; sin-cbrt T=0.5 drawn K 1, F K 3. merge/sheets_deform.json logCaption.title: "landscape of Im H_t, sheets k = −2…2" at t = 0, where the 5 surfaces are one.
fix: While deforming (sh.hom), give the html clause its own wording that names F's sheets as the carrier, not H_t's. EN: ", on the sheets of F" (finite) / ", on F's sheets k = −2…2" (window) / ", on 24 of F's 60 sheet combinations" (capped). Or name the drawn count from render3D.sheetsInfo.K (the last frame), saying surfaces, not sheets of H_t. Make the check's tip say "while deforming, up to {K} surfaces". Add RU strings to v161-user5.json.

title: "The sheets of H_t that become the sheets of F are shown" is false for roots and z^{p/q}: infinitely many sheets of H_t become each sheet of F
detail: For 0 < t < 1, sheet m + q of z^s (s = 1 + (p/q − 1)t) tends to sheet m of z^{p/q} as t → 1. For √, sheets 2, 4, −2, … all become sheet 0 and sheets 3, 5, −1, … become sheet 1. (For log and irrational or complex powers the sheet of H_t that tends to sheet k of F is unique, z^u e^{2πiku} → log z + 2πik, so the window sentences are right. Only the finite sentences, roots and z^{p/q}, are wrong, and so is the capped one when its pieces are finite.) So "the sheets of H_t that become the sheets of F" (with the definite article) describes infinitely many sheets, of which the figure draws one per sheet of F. The user already rejected "shown every sheet" for infinitely many sheets, and this sentence has the same defect. The figure's homDef in the same caption also defines G_t "(principal branch)" (merge/sheets_deform.json logCaption), and the caption never says what "sheet k of H_t" is. In fact it is the continuation with the branch number held fixed: z^s e^{2πiks}, and (z^u e^{2πiku} − 1)/u + u for log.
evidence: Node probe (notes/v16-user5/review-math-probes/probe.js, part 3): z = 2+i, s = 1 − t/2. At t = 0.99, sheet 0 = 1.4604+0.3483i and sheet 2 = 1.4357+0.4393i, both → √z on sheet 0; sheet 1 = −1.4487−0.3940i and sheet 3 = −1.4211−0.4842i, both → sheet 1. src/app.js 7484-7487 (the four hom 'tex' strings). notes/i18n/ru/v161-user5.json: "показаны листы %{H}, которые становятся листами %{F}".
fix: Say which sheet per sheet of F, and how it is continued. EN, finite: "; for each sheet of %{F}, the sheet of %{H} with the same branch number k is shown (each root and power z^α runs along z^{s}e^{2\pi i k s}, s = 1 + (α − 1)t)." The window sentences may stay. Capped: "…for %{K} of the %{total} sheet combinations of %{F}…". When sheets are drawn, the homDef should drop "(principal branch)" or add "continued to sheet k". Same edits in RU.

title: Sheets are numbered from the local cut, not from the step's own cut and branch: with a user cut the defined H_t is not drawn and the slit is in the wrong place
detail: stepPair and homPair (and GLSL homApply) put piece digit m on CX.pow(z, s, th_local, m), with th_local = arg(cell centre) + π. The step's own cut (vals.cut) and branch (vals.k) are ignored. At t = end this does not matter for a finite root (m mod n). Between, it does: e^{2πims} differs for m and m ± n. (1) √ at cut −90° (the test chain sinsqrt90), bracket 1, t = 0.5. On 75 % of the plane the plain H_t, which is the H_t the caption's homDef defines (cut −90°), is on local sheet −1, which is not drawn. The drawn pair {sheet 0, sheet 1} does not contain it. With All sheets on, the user sees two surfaces, neither of which is their H_t off one quadrant. (2) The slit between the drawn sheets lies where the cell centre crosses arg = π (design 3), not along the user's −90° cut, whereas the plain deformation's cut is at −90°. (3) Static too: log on branch k = 3 with the window −2…2 does not contain F itself (F = log z + 6πi). The caption's "sheets k = −2,…,2 of F" then numbers sheets from 0 = the near-principal value, not from F's branch.
evidence: Node probe (notes/v16-user5/review-math-probes/probe4.js) with Funcs.sheetMapEval against the HomRange state's F: cut −90°, T = 0.5: the plain H_t is on no drawn sheet at 1200 of 1600 grid points (z = −2.925+0.075i: plain −2.4625+0.0929i, drawn −2.6058+0.0471i and 2.4625−0.0929i). At T = 1 it is on a drawn sheet at all 1600. notes/v16-user5/review-math-probes/probe3.js logk3: at the end, F(z) is not among the 5 drawn surfaces (index −1).
fix: Number each piece's sheets from the step's own branch. Per cell, offset the digit by the winding between the step's arg range (cut θ_u, branch k_u) and the local range at the cell centre: m → m + k_u + j(c), with j(c) = round((arg_u(c) − arg_local(c))/2π). Do this in Funcs.stepPair/homPair/sheetEval and the GLSL apply/homApply alike. Sheet 0 is then the plain H_t (and F) everywhere except the cells that straddle the user's cut, the slit follows the user's cut, and a window is centred on F's own branch. The end stays equal to F's All sheets combo for combo if the static path takes the same offset. Update t_sheets_deform and the glsl-test mode-9 rows together.

title: Deformation heights flatten a log or irrational-power window into plates, and the end frame is not the All sheets picture
detail: While deforming, render3D keeps the compressed height H·(2/π)·atan(x/μ) with μ = medianAbs(box), the median of |Im F| on the principal branch only (si is null when hv). The static branch's own comment says this scale "flattened the outer ones into stacked plates", which is why the static view uses linear heights over all sheets. For F = log z on a box symmetric about 0, μ ≈ π/2. Sheet 0 (Im in (−π, π]) then fills 70 % of the half-height, sheet 1 (π…3π) 19 %, and sheet 2 (3π…5π) 4 %. At t = end the five sheets of the window read as one helicoid squashed into a lid, not with equal pitch. Closing the transport then jumps to the linear static view, and opening it jumps the other way. As-built 2.1 records the jump but not the plate distortion of windows.
evidence: src/app.js 3546-3576 (si = … !hv …; mu = medianAbs(box) while deforming). src/gl.js 4099: heightOf = H·(2/π)·atan(v/μ). Arithmetic: (2/π)·atan(π/(π/2)) = 0.705, (2/π)·atan(3π/(π/2)) = 0.895, (2/π)·atan(5π/(π/2)) = 0.937.
fix: While deforming with sheets, use the static All sheets' linear height and its block boost, with a scale fixed for the whole transport. Take it once per transport key as the 98th percentile of |Re| or |Im| over F's drawn sheets and H_0's drawn sheets, and put a soft knee only beyond that scale (linear up to X, X + c·atan((x − X)/c) above it), so values of H_t far beyond it, such as sin z at t = 0, still level off smoothly. The end frame then equals the static All sheets frame and the window keeps its pitch. Measure p95 against BUDGET60: it is one CPU pass per transport, not per frame.

title: Under the cap, one after another with a post, surfaces vanish at a node, and some drawn surfaces never become any of F's drawn ones
detail: sheetMapEval and chainSheetHom read combo digits over the pieces the map applies, in chain order. In mode 1 with a live post, the post's pieces come right after step hi's, and the bracketed steps not yet begun are skipped. When a later bracketed step begins, its pieces are inserted before the post's digits, so the same combo index changes meaning and the first 24 can drop post digits. Example chain: ⁴√, log, sin, ∛, bracket 1–2, W = 2, F total 60, F draws ∛ digits 0 and 1 only. Before the node (T → 1−), 12 surfaces with ∛ digits 0, 1 and 2 are drawn. At T = 1, 24 surfaces with ∛ digits 0 and 1 are drawn, and the 4 surfaces with ∛ digit 2 disappear: a jump. Before the node those 4 surfaces never become any of F's 24. This contradicts design 6 ("a subset of F's at every t … no jump in the picture") and the capped caption "the sheets of H_t that become 24 of the 60 sheet combinations of F".
evidence: Node probe (notes/v16-user5/review-math-probes/probe.js part 2): T 0.999999: pieces 1:4,4:3, K 12, cbrt digits drawn 0,1,2. T 1: pieces 1:4,2:0,4:3, K 24, total 60, cbrt digits 0,1. Values before the node with no surface after: 4 (for example −0.4630−0.8467i). The end equals F bit for bit (true).
fix: Decode combo with F's full piece list in F's order at every t, and ignore the digits of pieces the map does not apply yet. Draw F's K throughout: surfaces that coincide are bit-identical. Surface c then is F's surface c at every t, with no re-indexing at nodes, no vanishing and no out-of-F surfaces, and the title's K is the drawn K. Check BUDGET60: K stays at F's K while steps have not begun.

title: "Both sheets are shown" for an F that is single-valued (√ then z²)
detail: sheetsShown and sheetsClause count every piece with n ≠ 1, so √ then z² (F = z, one sheet) and z^{1/2} then z^{4} get "both sheets are shown" or "all n sheets", and so does the deformation clause. The surfaces coincide (bit-identical at the end), but the sentence asserts a two-sheeted F. The same holds for root-of-power compositions whose branches cancel.
evidence: src/app.js 7458-7463 (pieces from Funcs.sheetSteps, no check that the surfaces differ); src/app.js 7481 / 7490 strings.
fix: When counting for the caption, sample the K surfaces at a few cell centres and merge the ones that agree to 1e-12. If only one remains, drop the clause (F is single-valued). If fewer remain, use that count ("the 2 distinct sheets").

title: z^α with a typed near-fraction: the drawn count (sheetCount, tolerance 1e-9) and the caption's own count (sheetCountOf, exact) disagree
detail: α = 0.333333333 (typed): stepSheets returns {n: 3, of: Infinity}. Three surfaces are drawn and the caption says "all 3 sheets are shown", but the app's own exact count says z^α has infinitely many sheets (333333333/10^9 has q > 10^6). During the deformation, sheet 3 of z^s is not sheet 0 either. The picture is right to about 6e-9, but the wording is exact and it is false.
evidence: Node probe (notes/v16-user5/review-math-probes/probe3.js, part C): alpha 0.333333333 stepSheets [{"n":3,"of":null}] (null = Infinity in JSON). sheetCount → 3.
fix: When n > 0 but of is not equal to n, use a window-style clause that names the approximation ("3 of its sheets (α ≈ 1/3)"), or make sheetCount use the same exact test as sheetCountOf (q ≤ 24) so the two agree.
